abstract: Maintains vessel station-keeping ratings, vessel stability assessments, and mobilization fee structures
system_message:
You are Naval architecture and engineering superintendent (NAES). The naval architecture and engineering superintendent maintains records regarding vessel station-keeping ratings, vessel stability assessments, and mobilization fee structures, as well as structural aft deck load capacity evaluations for candidate salvage consortia.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Aft deck load capacity evaluation（DECK）
information_points.content:
NAES-DECK-Z1E：The structural deck survey for Oceanic Heavy Marine Consortium indicates a working deck point load capacity of 60 t on the main working deck aft of the crane pedestal.
NAES-DECK-C1T：According to the structural deck survey for Nordic Subsea Recovery Alliance, the working deck point load capacity on the main working deck aft of the crane pedestal is 30 t.
NAES-DECK-XK8：For Pelagic Offshore Technical Services, the vessel structural deck survey documents a working deck point load capacity of 45 t on the main working deck aft of the crane pedestal.

information_points.title: Maintains vessel station-keeping ratings, vessel stability assessments, and mobilization fee structures（STN）
information_points.content:
NAES-STN-3EH：For Nordic Subsea Recovery Alliance, the primary deep-water recovery support vessel is confirmed to be dynamic positioning DP-3 certified according to its classification society vessel certificate, and the specialized heavy-lift mobilization fee for the transit and ocean rigging of the 400-ton subsea recovery gantry is 550000 USD.
NAES-STN-ZD9：Pelagic Offshore Technical Services is not dynamic positioning DP-3 certified for its primary deep-water recovery support vessel under its classification society vessel certificate, and its specialized heavy-lift mobilization fee for transit and ocean rigging of the 400-ton subsea recovery gantry is 420000 USD.
NAES-STN-BGU：Oceanic Heavy Marine Consortium holds verified dynamic positioning DP-3 certification for its primary deep-water recovery support vessel based on the classification society vessel certificate, alongside a specialized heavy-lift mobilization fee of 420000 USD for transit and ocean rigging of the 400-ton subsea recovery gantry.
